text.p: A wildfire has forced the evacuation of dozens of homes and businesses and the closure of a highway along a scenic stretch of the California coast, officials said on Saturday.
The fire broke out on Friday afternoon in a canyon near the town of Big Sur, about 150 miles (240 kms) south of San Francisco.
One trailer has been destroyed but so far no homes have been lost and there have been no injuries, national forest spokesman Jim Youngson said.

The cause of the fire was not known. It burned up into the Ventana wilderness area of the Los Padres National Forest, an area famous for its natural beauty, and grew to 300 acres (120 hectares) by Saturday, Youngson said

The fire posed a threat to houses and businesses along Highway 1, a popular route that winds along the California coast, he said and added that all buildings east of the highway for a five-mile (8 km) stretch south from the Ventana Inn, have been evacuated.

About 25 homes and a half-dozen businesses, including the well-known Ventana Inn, which lies about two miles (3 kms) south of Big Sur, have been evacuated, he said. He did not know how many people were affected.
A 20-mile (30 km) section of Highway 1 has been closed to the public, although residents can get through, he said.
Youngson said there were campers and backpackers in the mountains and firefighters were trying to get to them as quickly as possible to warn them to leave the area.

About 900 firefighters were battling the blaze, backed by 43 fire engines, nine air tankers and eight helicopters, Youngson said. He said they were making a stand along a ridge road to try to stop the fire jumping over the road.
The fire was only five percent contained with no estimate of when it would be fully contained, Youngson said.

Ironically, the new fire broke out just about two hours before a 25,000-acre (10,000-hectare) blaze that had burned for 12 days about 30 miles (50 kms) away in the Los Padres National Forest was declared fully under control, Youngson said.
Because many firefighters were in the area, firefighters were able to quickly send a lot of resources to the new fire.
